author: massicomar
title: Removal Game
summary:
There is a list of $n$ numbers and two players who move alternately. On each move, a player removes either the first or last number from the list, and their score increases by that number. Both players try to maximize their scores.

What is the maximum possible score for the first player when both players play optimally?

Input

The first input line contains an integer $n$: the size of the list.

The next line has $n$ integers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$: the contents of the list.

Output

Print the maximum possible score for the first player.

constraints.text: n ≤ 5000 numbers; players alternately take the first or last

explanation: The remaining list is always a contiguous interval. Store the best (current player − opponent) difference per interval: O(n²).
traps: Greedily taking the larger end is not optimal.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[l][r] = best (my score − opponent's score) when the remaining list is l..r and it's my turn
dp[i] = best score for player 1 after i moves
options.why: After i moves you don't know which ends were taken.
Works, but the 'difference' formulation drops the turn dimension.

options.text: dp[mask] = best score with mask of taken numbers
options.why: 2^5000; also the taken set is always a prefix + suffix.

extraLayers.explanation: Whatever was taken, the rest is an interval; the difference trick makes the state symmetric for both players.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[l][r] = max(x_l − dp[l+1][r], x_r − dp[l][r−1]); answer = (total + dp[1][n]) / 2

options.why: Treats the opponent as if they help you; it ignores their moves.

options.text: dp[l][r] = max(x_l, x_r) + dp of the remaining interval
dp[l][r] = max over k of dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r]
options.why: Moves only remove an end; there's no split point.

extraLayers.explanation: Take an end, then the opponent faces the smaller interval and maximizes their own difference — subtract it.

es.explanation: Lo que queda de la lista siempre es un intervalo contiguo. Guarda la mejor diferencia (jugador actual − rival) por intervalo: O(n²).
traps: Tomar con greedy el extremo más grande no es óptimo.

dp-state.explanation: Se haya tomado lo que se haya tomado, lo que queda es un intervalo; el truco de la diferencia hace que el estado sea simétrico para los dos jugadores.

why.b: Después de i jugadas no sabes qué extremos se tomaron.
why.c: Funciona, pero la formulación con la “diferencia” elimina la dimensión del turno.
why.d: 2^5000; además, lo tomado siempre es un prefijo + un sufijo.

dp-transition.explanation: Toma un extremo; después el rival se enfrenta al intervalo más chico y maximiza su propia diferencia: réstala.

why.b: Trata al rival como si te ayudara; ignora sus jugadas.
why.d: Las jugadas solo sacan un extremo; no hay punto de corte.
